_comment: Price assumptions for the cost model. Every number has a source and an access date (all accessed 23.10.2026). Hardware is priced at current US retail prices for the same configuration, not at what the team paid, because both machines were bought earlier at lower prices and the RQ is about a team deciding today.
electricity_source: Astana-REK tariff for legal entities from June 2026: 39.58 KZT/kWh (digitalbusiness.kz, 26.05.2026); households pay 20.21 to 36.36 KZT/kWh
attribution_comment: dedicated = the machine is bought for inference and its whole price is charged to it. shared_dev_machine = the machine already exists as a developer workstation and only a quarter of its price is charged to inference (team assumption, stated in the report as a scenario, not a measurement).

mac_m4pro.source: Apple list price of MacBook Pro 14-inch, M4 Pro (12-core CPU, 16-core GPU), 24 GB, 512 GB: USD 1,999 (AppleInsider price guide, snapshot 01.07.2026)
mac_m4pro.load_watts_source: powermetrics CPU+GPU package power, mean over the concurrency-16 levels of the main run (runs/mac_m4pro/power_main_*.txt, results/power_by_level.csv); display and other components not included

Gigabyte UD750GM 750 W Gold: typical Amazon price reported by slickdeals.net, Jan 2026

pc_rtx4060.source: Sum of current US prices of the team's build without monitor and peripherals; see components_usd
pc_rtx4060.load_watts_source: nvidia-smi power.draw (GPU only) plus 80 W assumed for the rest of the system under load

AMD Ryzen 5 7600X: Amazon/Newegg early 2026 via slickdeals.net (177 to 210 USD)

pc_rtx4060_budget.source: Minimal inference box with the same GPU as the team's PC: mid-range CPU, B650 board, air cooling. Throughput and power are taken from the pc_rtx4060 measurements because all 33 layers run on the GPU and the CPU is almost idle during decoding; this is a cost scenario, not a separately measured machine.
pc_rtx4060_budget.load_watts_source: same GPU power log as pc_rtx4060 plus 60 W assumed for the rest of the system

rented_colab_gpu.source: Google Colab Pro: 19.99 USD per month for 100 compute units (colab.research.google.com/signup); compute units per hour of the L4 runtime are read from the Colab Resources panel during the run and entered here

mac_m4pro_q8.load_watts_source: powermetrics CPU+GPU package power, mean over the concurrency-16 levels of the main run (runs/mac_m4pro/power_main_*.txt, results/power_by_level.csv); display and other components not included
mac_m4pro_q8.note: same machine and price as mac_m4pro; measured separately

api_pricing_scenarios._comment: Applied in cost_model.py to hosted conditions without new runs. list = price billed in our runs. batch = Anthropic Message Batches at 50 percent of list (OpenRouter lists no ':batch' variant for meta-llama models, checked 23.10.2026), not usable for interactive chat. cache = prompt caching: Groq caches automatically and bills cached input at 0.5x; Anthropic needs cache_control and bills cache reads at 0.1x with a minimum cacheable prefix of 512 to 4,096 tokens depending on the model (OpenRouter prompt-caching docs, accessed 23.10.2026). Our prompts are 60 to 70 tokens with a 20-token system prompt, so the saving on our workload is zero; the scenario is computed for a hypothetical 1,500-token shared system prompt.
api_pricing_scenarios.sources: openrouter.ai/docs/features/prompt-caching; Anthropic pricing page; openrouter.ai/api/v1/models (batch variants), all accessed 23.10.2026
